title: Baker Mayfield: From Walk-On to the 2017 Heisman Trophy
question: Was Baker Mayfield a walk-on before winning the Heisman?
answer: Yes. Baker Mayfield walked on at Texas Tech in 2013 and again at Oklahoma, and in 2017 he became the first Heisman winner since scholarships began in the 1950s to start his college career as a walk-on.
summary: Baker Mayfield walked on at Texas Tech and then OU, set an NCAA passer rating record and won the 2017 Heisman before going No. 1 in the 2018 NFL draft.
body: Baker Mayfield's path to the Heisman began without a scholarship. A state champion at Lake Travis High near Austin, where he went 25-2 as a starter, he was passed over by most major programs and walked on at Texas Tech in 2013. He promptly became the first walk-on true freshman quarterback to start a season opener at the FBS level and threw for 413 yards in a win over SMU.

He then chose Oklahoma, again as a walk-on, and sat out 2014 under transfer rules. A dispute over his eligibility led Big 12 schools to vote in 2016 to amend the conference's walk-on transfer rule, a change fans quickly dubbed the Baker Mayfield rule.

On the field he only got better. Mayfield finished fourth in the Heisman voting in 2015 and third in 2016. In 2017 he completed 71 percent of his passes for 4,340 yards and 41 touchdowns in the regular season, with a 203.76 passer rating that set an NCAA record.

The 2017 vote was a landslide. Mayfield drew 732 first-place votes, led every voting region and totaled 2,398 points, more than Stanford's Bryce Love and Louisville's Lamar Jackson combined. The Heisman Trust notes he was the first winner to begin his college career as a walk-on since scholarships arrived in the 1950s.
The Cleveland Browns made him the first overall pick of the 2018 NFL draft. He later played for Carolina and the Los Angeles Rams before signing with Tampa Bay in 2023.
